title: Publish existing reviewed local history to an empty GitHub repository

location.start: Begin at About importing source code, read the warning, then use Initializing a Git repository and Adding a local repository to GitHub using Git.
location.stop: Stop after the first verified push; do not use history rewriting, migration tools, GitHub CLI automation, GitHub Desktop, organizations, or paid features.
location.note:
Do: Initialize `main`, stage explicit reviewed files, commit, create a GitHub repository without README/license/gitignore initialization, add and verify origin, then push. Record status before staging, after staging, and after push.

title: Prevent generated and sensitive files from entering history

location.start: Find Avoiding accidental commits in the future and read only its preventive bullet list.
location.stop: Stop before removing existing history, revoking real credentials, support tickets, collaborator cleanup, forks, and `git-filter-repo`; those are incident response, not this clean publication path.
location.note:
Do: Ignore `.exe`, `.o`, editor caches, secrets, and real data; stage explicit source/docs/sample paths; run `git status --short` and `git diff --cached`; if a private file appears, unstage it, correct the ignore/sample rule, and inspect again.

Finished when: The final staged and published set contains source, docs, checks, and sanitized sample data—but no generated output, secret, or real learner record.

Next: Take the Week 8 Skill Check, complete LabTrack, and verify the public repository from a fresh clone.

whySelected: The official prevention guidance explicitly recommends `.gitignore`, avoiding catch-all staging, individually reviewing files, and inspecting the cached diff before publication.
